out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

out_items.name: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction

violations.title: Shellstock Removed from Tagged or Labeled Container
violations.observation: Shellstock has been removed from the tagged/labeled container without preserving source identification. OBSERVED RAW MUSSELS IN A PREP-TOP COOLER WITHOUT THE TAG.
violations.corrective_action: Shellstock that has been removed from the tagged/labeled container must have a system used to identify source. CDI: PIC PUT THE TAG WITH THE MUSSELS. ENSURE THE TAG IS ALWAYS KEPT WITH SHELLSTOCK UNTIL THE SHELLSTOCK IS GONE.

violations.title: Shellstock Label Marked, Last Date Served/Sold Info
violations.observation: The date when the last shellstock from the container is sold or served is not CONSISTENTLY recorded on the tag or label.
violations.corrective_action: The identity of the source of shellstock (oysters, clams, mussels) that are sold or served shall be maintained by retaining shellstock tags or labels and marking the tag or label with the date when the last shellstock from the container is sold or served. CDI: PIC RE-EDUCATED. ENSURE THE DATE THE LAST PIECE OF SHELLSTOCK IS USED FROM THE BATCH IS WRITTEN ON THE APPLICABLE TAG.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: OBSERVED RAW SHELL EGG STORED ON A SHELF ABOVE BREAD IN THE ONE-DOOR STANDING COOLER.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. CDI: EGGS MOVED BELOW THE BREAD. PIC RE-EDUCATED.

out_items.name: Proper hot holding temperatures

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: OBSERVED IN STEAM TABLE: CRAB DIP AT 126F, SPINACH DIP AT 121F. PIC STATED FOODS WERE PUT INTO STEAM TABLE 1HR PRIOR. NEAT STOVE: COOKED ONIONS AT 88F (1HR)

CDI: FOODS MOVED TO STOVE TO REHEAT TO 165F. PIC RE-EDUCATED ON NOT DOUBLE PANNING FOODS IN THE STEAM TABLE. COOKED ONIONS MOVED TO FREEZER TO RAPID COOL. violations.corrective_action: Corrected by discarding. Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: hard boiled eggs, pasta, mashed potatoes, roasted vegetables
violations.corrective_action: Corrected by instruction. Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: several containers of cooked peppers observed on counter to cool and 5gal container of clam soup observed cooling in walk-in.
violations.corrective_action: Please not the following: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

out_items.name: Food properly labeled, original container

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: sugar, flour, oil, balsamic glaze, graham cracker crust.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc.

Routinely inspect the premises to control the presence of insects, rodents and pests on the premises.

out_items.name: Approved thawing methods used

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: Spinach thawing in the prep sink under standing water.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. EHS informed PIC that thawing is required to take place under running water or in a cooler, PIC turned on water for prep sink.

violations.title: Thermometers, Location for Units with TCS foods
violations.observation: There was no temperature measuring device located in the following cold or hot holding equipment: 4 drawer prep top across from deep fat fryers, and 4 drawer prep top across from flat top grill.
violations.corrective_action: Cold or hot holding equipment used for the storage of time/temperature control for safety food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one integral or permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display. PCI replaced thermometers for cold holding units missing thermometers.
